subChunks.title: Functional Interfaces & Lambdas

storyBeats.text: Eldrin holds up an ancient scroll — 20 lines of incantation for one trivial effect. Then he holds up a modern rune: a single line that does the same thing.

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: A lambda is condensed arcane notation. Where once you wrote an entire anonymous invocation ritual, you now write the essence: the parameters and what to do with them. The compiler infers the rest.

storyBeats.label: Lambda basics

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Note the :: — a method reference. String::length is shorthand for the lambda s -> s.length(). Where a lambda merely calls an existing method, a method reference is cleaner.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Create a Predicate<String> that tests if a string starts with "A". Create a Function<String, String> that converts to uppercase. Test both on "Arcane" and "magic".
guidedPractice.hint: Use s -> s.startsWith("A") for the Predicate. Use s -> s.toUpperCase() or String::toUpperCase for the Function.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: What is a functional interface? Describe the four main functional interfaces in java.util.function and give an example of each.

questions.prompt: How many abstract methods can a functional interface have?
questions.explanation: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method — this is what allows it to be implemented by a lambda or method reference.

questions.prompt: A lambda expression can be used anywhere a functional interface is expected.
questions.explanation: Lambdas implement functional interfaces. Wherever you need a functional interface instance, you can supply a lambda that matches the single abstract method's signature.

subChunks.title: Method References & Composing Functions

storyBeats.text: Eldrin points to a spell book entry that says 'cast upperCase'. 'Why write a whole new incantation for that?' he asks. 'Just reference the one that already exists.'

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Method references are the lazy wizard's best friend — in the complimentary sense. When your lambda body is simply call this method, a method reference makes it unmistakably clear.

storyBeats.label: Method references

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Composing functions is building spell chains. andThen links them sequentially: the output of one flows into the next. Predicate.and() and .or() combine boolean tests without nested ifs.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Use method references to: (1) parse "42" to int using Integer::parseInt, (2) convert "hello" to uppercase using String::toUpperCase. Print both results.
guidedPractice.hint: Function<String, Integer> parse = Integer::parseInt; and Function<String, String> upper = String::toUpperCase;

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Describe the four types of method reference in Java. Give an example of each and explain when you would use a method reference instead of a lambda.

questions.prompt: names.forEach(System.out::println) — which type of method reference is this?
options: Instance method of a particular object
Instance method of an arbitrary object
questions.answer: Instance method of a particular object
questions.explanation: System.out is a specific PrintStream instance. System.out::println is an instance method reference on that specific object.
